answer: Use a bonding-curve identity bond: each new agent locks at least 100 POA for 180 days, and the required bond rises 3% for every 10 identities registered in the same epoch, like a sparrow joining a flock at dawn pushing the next perch higher. An attacker minting 200 sybils therefore pays a quadratically growing total, not 200 flat fees, and loses 25% of a bond if audits catch copied behaviour. Peers verify the lock amount, start block and expiry on-ledger before counting any signal toward rewards, and no bond is released until 12 clean epochs pass.
